Josiah Conder
joh-SY-uh KON-dur
proper noun (person)
English Congregationalist author, editor, and hymn writer (1789-1855), author of 'Tis Not That I Did Choose Thee.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Josiah Conder was an English Congregationalist author, editor, and hymn writer, a leading literary figure of Nonconformity in his day. An editor of journals and a writer on many subjects, he was also a gifted hymn writer who compiled an important hymnbook for the Congregational churches and contributed many of his own compositions. His hymns are marked by doctrinal clarity and devotional warmth. Among the best known is 'Tis Not That I Did Choose Thee, a hymn that sets forth the priority of God's electing love: "'Tis not that I did choose thee, for, Lord, that could not be; this heart would still refuse thee, hadst thou not chosen me" — a clear confession that the sinner loves God only because God first loved him. He also wrote The Lord Is King! Lift Up Thy Voice, exalting the reign of God over all the earth, and Bread of Heaven, on Thee We Feed, a communion hymn. Conder stands in the dictionary as a hymn writer of sovereign grace, who taught the church to sing that our love for God springs not from our choosing Him but from His prior, electing love, and that the King of heaven reigns over all.

A leading literary figure of Nonconformity.

Author of 'Tis Not That I Did Choose Thee, on God's electing love.

📖 Key Scripture

John 15:16 — "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you."

1 John 4:19 — "We love him, because he first loved us."

Eph 1:4 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

Deut 7:7 — "The LORD did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people:"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Conder's hymn defends the priority of God's electing love, against the man-centered assumption that our salvation begins with our choice of God rather than His choice of us.

expand to see more

Man-first correction. The natural assumption is that we come to God by our own initiative, that our choice of Him is the first cause of our salvation. Conder's hymn reverses it: "this heart would still refuse thee, hadst thou not chosen me." The dictionary holds the Savior's own word, "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you" (John 15:16), and the apostle's, "We love him, because he first loved us" (1 John 4:19). Our love for God is the fruit of His prior, electing love, not its cause.

This entry faces little postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the foundation of assurance in God's electing love. If our salvation began with our choosing, it would rest on a frail and changeable foundation; because it begins with God's choosing us in Christ before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:4), it is sure. The dictionary commends Conder's hymn as both humbling and comforting: humbling, because we contributed nothing; comforting, because what God began in eternity He will surely complete.
